title: Velocity targeter: scaling limiter with tokenized throughput contracts
creator: Ana Patel
description: Implement a policy engine component — the Velocity Targeter — that expresses scaling intent in terms of token/throughput contracts and enforces a slope-limited scaling limiter. The component will convert high-level throughput guarantees (tokens/s per tenant or route) into scaling requests for the autoscaler, apply safety fences (max step, min headroom, surge budget), and provide deterministic rollback behavior. Goal: allow Dedicated customers to declare throughput contracts and have predictable, safe autoscaling that preserves latency SLOs and cost bounds.
acceptance_criteria: Velocity Targeter accepts a throughput_contract object per tenant and route and emits a scaling_intent event every evaluation window
Scaling intent includes target_tokens_per_sec, desired_replica_count, confidence_interval (p50/p95 demand forecast) and a safety_annotation (max_step, min_headroom, surge_credit)

Autoscaler applies the scaling intent and never increases fleet capacity by more than max_step_percent per 2m window (configurable); documented integration tests simulate bursts and assert constraint holds
When capacity is constrained, targeter automatically degrades to a configured contingency model (serve using a compatible lower-capacity model variant) and logs the reason and affected tenants
End-to-end e2e test shows 99.9% of requests for a protected tenant meet latency SLO when scaling policy is active under synthetic load up to 3x baseline
design_decisions: Use a hybrid control algorithm: predictive quantile demand forecast (LightGBM-based) + conservative PI controller for final target to balance responsiveness and oscillation avoidance
Emit scaling_intent as an idempotent event into the existing scaling bus (topic 'scaling-intent.v1') to reuse the orchestrator and audit trails
Represent throughput contracts as tokenized objects (tokens/second + priority class + minimum_committed_capacity) to enable deterministic merging and credits
Safety fences implemented as layered checks: (1) per-evaluation max_step, (2) fleet-wide surge_budget accounting ledger, (3) tenant min_headroom floor computed from baseline p95 latency traces
Fallback path for private deployments: local targeter runs with a shorter evaluation window and exposes a read-only admin endpoint for manual overrides
technical_notes: Evaluation window default: 30s for prediction sampling, 120s for enforcement horizon; both configurable via runtime flags
Forecast model inputs: per-tenant token rate time-series, route-specific latency p95, scheduled events, recent warmup credits; output p50/p95 demand forecast for next 2m and 10m windows
PI controller gains tuned conservatively in staging (Kp=0.6, Ki=0.15 for typical tokenized workloads) with automatic backoff when oscillation metric crosses threshold
Max_step expressed as percent of current fleet capacity (default 20% per 2m) to support gradual expansion and reduce token cache thrashing
Surge budget uses integer 'credits' banked when load below contract; credits decay with half-life configurable per tenant (default 6h)
Scaling intents carry causal metadata: request_id, forecast_window, model_version, last_applied_intent_id for reconciliation and safe rollbacks
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind 'velocity-targeter' guard, disabled by default for existing fleets
Week 1: Smoke rollout to internal staging fleets with synthetic tokenized workloads; validate scaling_intent format and audit logs
Week 2: Canary to 3 non-critical customers with opt-in contracts; monitor latencies, tail SLOs, and surge_budget accounting
Week 3: Expand to 30% of Dedicated fleets with conservative max_step defaults; run A/B comparing cost per token and latency regression
Full enablement after 4 weeks and validation against acceptance criteria; provide migration script for older contract formats
test_plan: Unit tests: forecasting component, PI controller, safety fence algebra, surge ledger accounting
Integration tests: inject synthetic load spike (1s-10s bursts) and assert max_step and surge credit behavior
E2E chaos tests: simulate node failures and verify targeter recalculates desired_replicas without violating min_headroom
Performance tests: bench evaluation loop at 10k tenants to confirm decision latency < 200ms
Regression: run against the autoscaler simulator used by ENG-77222 and compare step profiles to baseline
monitoring_and_alerting: Alerts: intent_emission_failures > 5 in 5m, oscillation_detector firing more than 3 times in 15m (investigate parameter drift), surge_budget_depletion for gold tenants
Audit logs: every scaling_intent persisted to audit store with reason and causal metadata for postmortems
migration_notes: Backward-compatibility: convert legacy throughput ACLs to throughput_contract using a one-time migration job; keep support for min_committed_replicas field
Customers with manual autoscaler overrides will be opted out by default; operators can opt-in per-tenant via Console or API
Documented CLI shim: rwdctl targeter preview --tenant T-123 --window 120s to show expected intent without applying
